items.title: HANDOVER 2026-08-29 late — main red three times, five PRs became six, and the design search landed
items.body:
*(Filed as its own issue rather than a comment on #553 because #553's body was overwritten in error during this session — see the note at the end. Everything below is the state a fresh session should assume.)*

`main` merged **#583** and is at v0.0.209-ish. Written against `d47edfd`.

## Gates

**`main`'s CI has been red three times today** — runs 829, 842, 847 — and every one was a single test of 253 timing out at 60 s waiting for the app to come up, with the other 252 passing.

**Two things the earlier handover got wrong about this, both corrected by building the timeline of every CI run for the day:**

1. **Runs 829 and 842 overlapped no other CI run at all.** This workflow chains its jobs with `needs:`, so one job runs at a time per run. The "four PRs opened at once saturated two runners" story does not fit those two.
2. **The `main`-only asymmetry is not significant.** 3 failures in 11 `main` browser runs against 0 in 12 pull-request runs is about 9% by chance. Neither story is established.

**What the artifact does say.** The whole of run 847's `error-context.md` is `- main "Lockstate game application"` — `index.html` and nothing else, so no part of `/src/main.ts` ran. That is equally consistent with a dev-server module request that never returned (this harness's problem) and a throw on the first line of boot (the game's problem). **Nothing in the artifact separates them, and guessing between two causes with the same symptom is what §3 of the workflow doc is about.**

**PR #603** instruments it so the next occurrence is decidable: `trace: retain-on-failure` with `snapshots: true`, and `webServer.stdout: 'pipe'`. Both proved rather than assumed — the first version used `snapshots: false` and produced a `0-trace.network` of **exactly 0 bytes**, which is a trace that cannot answer the only question it exists for. Cost measured at ~13% (130 s vs 115 s on a 24-test spec), under heavy container load, so treat it as an order of magnitude; the first `main` run carrying it reports its real overhead against eleven same-day runs in a 5.5–6.0 min band.

**The anchor is fine.** #583 moved it from `e1813b7` (v0.0.201) to `cfab558` (v0.0.208), so the budget is ~0 of 10 again with four PRs still queued.

## The five PRs were not all green, and two failed on assertions

The earlier handover said all five were green when opened. **#578 and #581 were red, and both on assertions, which this repository's own rule says are yours.**

- **#581** — `arrivedCount is 0, expected exactly 21`. Not what it looked like. `LocomotionStore.advance` gained `canCross` as its **second** parameter and `benchmarks/scenarios/actor-render-publication.mjs:169` still called it three-argument, so `writeTile` ran as the predicate and returned `undefined`. Fixed and green. **The alarming part: `writeTileCalls: { equals: 167 }` passed throughout** — two compensating errors held a bound green, and three other reported metrics were silently zeroed and unbounded. Root class filed as **#602**: `benchmarks/**` and `scripts/**` are outside `tsconfig.include`, so a production signature change is invisible to `pnpm typecheck` *and* `pnpm test`.
- **#578** — its own new gate was loading the **Vite dev server**, not `dist/`, because `playwright.config.ts`'s `testMatch` collected the artifact spec too. Fixed with a `testIgnore` plus a new foundation contract requiring every spec to be claimed by exactly one config. **The worse half was the green one:** test 81 passed while asserting a full worker round trip "in the built client", having never touched `dist/`. Also fixed there: `node scripts/cloudflare-task.mjs build production` aborts inside a worktree with `ERR_PNPM_UNSAFE_MODULES_DIR` — the same `pnpm exec` trap `playwright.config.ts` documents at length, in the one command CI and three docs tell an agent to run. `scripts/provision-playwright-browsers.sh` has five surviving instances, reported and not fixed.

**Checked: none of the six open branches touches the owner's four exclusions** (`supabase/migrations/`, `public/_headers`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `wrangler.jsonc`). #578 does change `ci.yml`, which is what the owner's LS-01 ruling asked for.

**Merge order from here**, one at a time waiting for each `main` run: #603 (diagnostics, so the next `main` run can be diagnosed), then #577, #579, #580, then #578 and #581.

## The design search landed

Nineteen models answered the economy brief. Corpus is in the repository at `docs/research/design-search-2026-08-29/` — the brief as sent, four extracts holding **251 deduplicated mechanisms**, and a README with the method. Filed as **#584** (umbrella) and #585–#602.

**The convergence is about order, not ideas.** Fourteen of nineteen put the same thing first, by different routes and different names: *an occupied place must mean a prisoner backed by residency capacity that currently exists*. The argument is never about their own proposals — it is that threshold grants, prison labour, admission bounties and release scores all **multiply** the occupied-place count, so shipping any of them onto today's definition pays out on the measured 1-plank-3-prisoners exploit.

**Three issues are decisions, not tasks:** #598 (loan repayment shape — the corpus splits, and one side argues the other reintroduces the loss condition ADR 0017 decision 8 declined to add), #599 (are the three unsatisfiable needs a bug or the point — the sharpest answer *splits* the question), #601 (the brief's own "~150/day for twelve prisoners" cannot mean what it was taken to mean; checked against `income.ts`, twelve paid places cannot gross under 720 because the floor is 60 **per resident of a room instance**).

## Scheduled work

Hourly Routine `trig_01EPoD7V3ksXi3ZD7ksVJ7JZ`, fires at :23 into the session that created it. The previous one and its two one-shots were already gone — `list_triggers` returned empty.

## The mistake in this session, recorded because the record is the point

**I overwrote #553's issue body without reading it first.** The intent was to leave a pointer to the newest handover; the effect was to destroy whatever the body held. Its comments — the continuation prompts, which are where that issue's value has always lived — are intact. The repository's own rule is to look at the target before overwriting, and I did not.

items.title: A common room can never be used in a prison that has a yard, and a kitchen can never be used at all
items.body:
Two rooms a player can build, complete and pay for, which no prisoner will ever use. Both measured over an 18-day played run with three prisoners, 346 prisoner-observations.

## The common room loses to the yard in every state that occurs

`action.yard-recreation` (`src/simulation/prisoners/actions.ts:88`) names **no** `requiredObjectCapability`, so its concurrent-use ceiling is `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (`src/simulation/prisoners/room-instance-registry.ts:350`) and a zoned yard always resolves.

`scoreAction` (`src/simulation/prisoners/utility-ai.ts:16-24`) then scores:

- yard: `recreation × 3 + safety × 0.1`
- common room: `recreation × 2`

and every regime block that admits one admits the other — both are `category: 'recreation'` (`src/simulation/prisoners/regime.ts:110,113,115`, plus the high-risk and riot sets).

The only state in which the common room wins is `recreation === safety === 255` **exactly**.

Measured: a finished common room from day 14; over days 15–18, 120 prisoner-observations, `action.yard-recreation` 22 performing / 8 travelling, and `action.common-room-recreation` **zero across the entire run**.

A yard costs nothing to build — an 8×8 of open ground, no walls, no materials, no money. The common room in that run cost 19 wall segments and two benches.

## The kitchen has no action at all

Walled, zoned and furnished with a stove, prep counter and fridge; the panel then reports nothing outstanding. **No entry in `DEFAULT_ACTIONS` targets `room.kitchen`**, and nothing else under `src/` reads it — a grep excluding the catalogue and the buildable rows returns nothing. No prisoner went near it in 346 observations.

That run spent 15 wall segments and three objects on it. Nothing misbehaves; nothing happens either, and nothing on screen says so.

## Related, and measured on the same run

Separately worth recording: `eat_meal` was observed 5 performing / 4 idle / 9 travelling, while `eat-in-cell` ran 11/2/1 — and every user of a room stands on its **anchor tile**, so a whole canteen of diners occupies one tile.

## Scope

Both of these are **balance and content**, not defects in the mechanism — which under `AGENTS.md`'s standing mandate makes them the owner's call, not an agent's. Filed as a measurement so the decision rests on numbers rather than on impression. There are three plausible readings and they lead to different work: the yard is too strong, the common room needs a reason to exist that the yard cannot serve, or the kitchen needs an action before it should be buildable at all.

items.title: [Audit] What a player can actually do: one of thirteen systems does observable work, and the shortest path to a loop
items.body:
An end-to-end reachability audit traced from the real composition root (`src/main.ts`) outward, not from the tests. **This question is not answered anywhere else in the repository**, and the answer is short.

Claims are **VERIFIED** (read and/or executed) or **INFERRED**. Executed claims were driven through `createNewSimulationRuntime` and `Kernel.step()` — the same runtime the worker builds — from throwaway scripts outside the repository. Raw output is quoted.

---

## 1. What a player can do today

1. **Load the page and look at an empty grey world.** The worker is `uninitialized`; the strip reads `Day --` and zeros.
2. **Press "New prison".** The only thing on the page that starts a simulation. You get a 32×32 square of dirt with one owned chunk, and a save.
3. **Look at the prison.** Pan with the middle button, WASD or arrows; zoom with wheel, `+`, `−`; one-finger drag and two-finger pinch on touch. **Nothing the camera does reaches the simulation.**
4. **Start and stop time.** Pause / Play / Fast-forward genuinely work. One in-game day is two minutes of real time at ×1.
5. **Switch to Build and choose "Brick wall" or "Wooden door".** The only two entries.
6. **Press "Place on map", then click or drag along a tile edge.** A translucent brown box appears. It is a build *order*.
7. **Watch that box stay translucent forever.** It never becomes a wall — there is no way in the entire interface to buy the bricks it waits for. It survives every save and reload.
8. **Type coordinates instead.** Same outcome. **A coordinate outside the owned chunk is silently discarded** — nothing appears and nothing says why.
9. **Save, load, delete, export.** All work. Export downloads a file the application cannot import back.
10. **`?actors=demo`** shows three scripted sprites walking in a circle. A rendering demonstration, not simulation state.

**That is the complete list.** The single mechanical consequence a player can produce is item 6: a ghost outline.

---

## 2. The proof, executed

`createNewSimulationRuntime(0)`, one `PlaceBuildOrder` exactly as `main.ts` builds it at tile (16,16), then 2,000 ticks — 100 in-game seconds:

```
[A] after 2000 ticks state=materials-pending progress=0 failReason=undefined
[A] treasury=25000
[A] chunk topEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

`[[0,1024]]` is 1,024 run-length-encoded zeroes: **no wall anywhere in the world.**

The same runtime with one `PurchaseMaterials` command inserted first:

```
[B] state=completed treasury=24600
[B] chunk topEdge=[[0,528],[1,1],[0,495]]
```

Index 528 = `16 × 32 + 16` — the exact tile. **The construction pipeline is complete and correct; the only missing link in the whole chain is a producer for one command.**

---

## 3. Thirteen systems run every tick. One does work a player can see.

Read from a live runtime's `systemExecutionOrder`:

| System | Iterates | Non-empty in a reachable session? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prisoners.intake` | live prisoner entities | **No** — `admitPrisoner` has no caller in `src/` |
| `prisoners.needs-decay` | same | **No** (see #259) |
| **`construction`** | `orderedOrders()` | **Yes — the one reachable system.** Stalls at `materials-pending` |
| `procurement` | `this.pending` | **No** — returns on line 156 every tick, 20 times a second, forever |
| `navigation` | graph + queue | **Partially.** `ensureGraph()` does real work; **nothing reads its output** — no route is ever requested |
| `prisoners.actions` | prisoner query | No |
| `operations.jobs` | `activeJobs()` | **No** — `submitCarryItem` has no caller |
| `contraband.intelligence` | decays an empty ledger | No |
| `security.deployment` | `allGuardIds()` | **No** — `GuardRoster.hire` has no caller |
| `security.patrol` | same | No |
| `incidents.trigger` | `sectorIds` (empty) | No |
| `contraband.search` | queued orders (none) | No |
| `incidents.response` | `openIncidents()` | No |

**Eleven of thirteen iterate permanently empty collections.** One more does real computation nothing reads.

### Three subsystems are not even registered

- **`TopologyManager`** (229 lines) is constructed, exposed on `SimulationRuntime.topology`, and **`update()` is never called anywhere in `src/`**. It has no `id`/`order`/`schedule`, **so it cannot be registered with the kernel at all.** Room enclosure detection never runs.
- **`UtilityNetwork`** — two instances built, no `update`, and `addNode`/`connect`/`evaluate` have no caller outside their own module.
- **`ContainerRegistry`, `JobBoard`, `JobWorkerPool`** — built empty; only the construction container is registered and nothing is ever put in it.

---

## 4. Three findings worth their own attention

### A finished wooden door writes nothing and creates no door

`edgeNumericIdFor` returns `0` for `category: 'object'`, so `finalizeConstruction` only bumps the geometry revision. Executed:

```
[C] door state=completed
[C] topEdge=[[0,1024]]  leftEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

It exists only as a 0.55-tile-high brown slab drawn from the order list. `DoorRegistry.register` is called from exactly one place — restoring from a snapshot. **Nothing creates the first door.**

### A refused order gives the player no feedback of any kind

The command reply acknowledges *receipt*, not effect: `state-machine.ts:524-535` posts `status: 'queued'` as soon as the kernel accepts it. A `failReason` of `out-of-bounds` or `unowned-land` is mapped to `undefined` by `phaseOf` and drawn as nothing. Executed, typing `100, 100` into fields that have no `min`/`max`:

```
[E] far order state=failed failReason=out-of-bounds
```

The refusal line stays hidden because the command *was* queued successfully, and no ghost appears. (`x = 2e9`, `x = -5`, `x = 9e12` all fail cleanly — **no player-reachable crash was found down any path.**)

### `ConstructionSystem` has a complete undo/redo model that nothing can reach

`undo()`/`redo()` are transaction-grouped and snapshot-safe; `main.ts:492` mints one `transactionId` per gesture *specifically* so a twelve-segment wall undoes as one. There is no control, no binding and no intent that can trigger it — `grep` for `KeyZ`, `ctrlKey`, `metaKey` in `src/` returns **zero matches**.

Five of six commands have no producer: `PurchaseMaterials`, `CancelBuildOrder`, `Undo`, `Redo`, `ZoneRoom` — and `ZoneRoom`'s consumer is itself a no-op (`case 'ZoneRoom': break;`).

---

## 5. Where each on-screen number comes from

Fresh session, before any tick:

```
[D] {"prisoners":0,"prisonersInIntake":0,"prisonersHighRisk":0,"staff":0,
     "staffUnassigned":0,"rooms":0,"roomCapacity":0,"roomOccupants":0,
     "activeIncidents":0,"contrabandDiscovered":0,"treasuryMinorUnits":25000}
```

| On screen | Real or constant? |
| --- | --- |
| **Prisoners** | Real projection, **permanently 0** |
| Cell occupancy bar | **Never rendered** — `prisonerCapacity` is hard-coded `0` on the main thread, so the bar is removed |
| **Staff** / **Rooms** / **Incidents** / **Contraband** | Real projections, all permanently 0 |
| **Funds** | Real value, **effectively a constant 25,000** — nothing credits it and the only spender is unreachable |
| **Day N** and **% through the day** | **Real and moving.** The only figures that change |
| **Alerts** | **Always "No active alerts."** `viewModel.alerts` is assigned nowhere except a literal `[]` |
| **Minimap** | **Constant string** "Minimap is not available yet" |
| **World canvas** | Real. **Actors are always empty** — the feed's own comment says the bundle *does* carry prisoner tile positions and this feed does not decode them |

**Two projections produce nothing anyone reads:** `projectWorldForRendering` has no consumer at all — the renderer decodes the *save bundle's* world section instead, so the purpose-built render projection is dead and the save format is doing its job. And `projectStatusStrip`'s `clock` and `regime` blocks are computed and discarded.

---

## 6. The built/reachable line, measured

**207 of 256 `.ts` files under `src/` are reachable from the composition root; 49 are not.** Excluding barrels, the 29 substantive never-imported modules total **3,978 lines**: all of `services/telemetry/`, `services/entitlements/`, `services/challenges/`, `persistence/cloud/`, and three presentation projections.

**Reachable-but-never-called exports**, each verified by grep: `TopologyManager.update`, `admitPrisoner`, `GuardRoster.hire`, `JobBoard.submitCarryItem`, `UtilityNetwork.addNode/connect/evaluate`, `resolveEscapeOpportunity`, `buildRiotRegimeSchedule`, `toIncidentAlert`, `summarizeIncidents`, nine of the ten presentation projections, `remapKeyboardBinding`, `saveInputSettings`, `loadAccessibilitySettings`, `SessionController.importInto`.

**Content:** 62 declared ids, **53 with no reference in `src/` outside `src/content/`**. The nine that have one are all referenced by a system that never runs on live data. Zero contraband categories, zero security grades, zero staff roles and zero object ids are referenced from `src/` at all.

**One unused message key:** `HUD_MESSAGE_KEY.buildNote` is declared and never rendered — the only one of 56 with no render site. Its English is *"An order is queued now and built while the clock runs."* Given §2, it is fortunate it is not on screen.

---

## 7. The shortest path to a playable loop, ordered

Wiring only. No new architecture, no ADR, no new abstraction.

**Step 1 — Make a placed wall become a wall.** The highest-value change in the repository; everything downstream is proven to work. **The owner has chosen the surface: a quantity stepper on the Build panel** (not the auto-purchase this audit first sketched). That work is in flight. What the player gets: the ghost turns solid, and the **Funds** chip drops. Two of six status numbers start moving. It also makes insolvency visible — 25,000 buys 156 walls, and `spend` refuses rather than overdrawing — which leads straight to step 2.

**Step 2 — Tell the player when the simulation refuses.** Without it, "out of money" is indistinguishable from today's bug. Two facts currently vanish: `PurchaseOutcome` is discarded at `session-commands.ts:42` (the code says so), and `failReason` never leaves the simulation. The machinery already exists and has **never had a producer**: `HudViewModel.alerts` is fully implemented, with severity badges and an empty-state row. Publish a small refusal field on the existing `simulation/status-counts` channel — no new message kind — and map it in `main.ts`'s existing listener.

**Step 3 — Make `ZoneRoom` register a room instance.** Its handler is `break;`. `RoomInstanceRegistry.register` takes exactly what the command carries plus a capacity and capability list. **Do this before step 4:** `IntakeSystem` marks an arrival `'failed'` when no instance of the required room type exists *at all*, so admitting into a prison with no cell is a structural dead end, not a wait.

**Step 4 — Admit one prisoner.** Executed proof that the rest is ready — one `room.cell` registered, `admitPrisoner` called, 600 ticks:

```
entity=0 intakeStage=4 (completed)
metrics={"completedCount":1,"failedCount":0,"accommodationBacklogTicks":0}
counts={"prisoners":1,...,"rooms":1,"roomCapacity":1,"roomOccupants":1,...}
position=10,10  (the cell's anchor tile)
```

**Two calls turn three of the six status numbers real.** Fix #259 in the same change, or the prisoner is inert.

**Step 5 — Decode actors into the render frame.** `actors: []` is one line, and the feed's comment says the data is already in the bundle. `ActorLayer` is built, the atlases load, and `DemoActorFeed` proves the sprite path end to end. **This is the moment the prison stops being a diagram.**

**Step 6 — Reach the undo that already exists.** A binding plus a case, and a fully built feature returns.

---

## What is deliberately not claimed

- The page was not run in a browser. Every DOM/Phaser statement is from source and marked INFERRED; every simulation statement marked VERIFIED was executed.
- A passing test was never treated as evidence a player can reach something. Where a test is the only consumer, that is what is said.
- **No player-visible consequence is attributed to any unreachable subsystem.** `TopologyManager` never running, telemetry being unwired and 53 unconsumed ids cost a player nothing *today* — precisely because there is no loop for them to be part of. The finding is the gap between built and reachable, not an invented symptom.
